business_overview: This queue entry tracks a ValuePickr thematic thread on India's battery energy storage (BESS) buildout and whether solar+BESS round-the-clock (RTC) / firm-dispatchable (FDRE) structures threaten or replace discom-style peaking power. It is not a single listed company -- a prior pass (2026-09-26 four-box correction) already flagged it as 'a thematic placeholder not a single ticker.' This full-dive pass confirms that remains the case: the thread's named proxies (ACME Solar, KPI Green Energy, Pace Digitek, Enviro Infra Engineers, Inox Wind/Inox Green/Inox Clean Energy) span fundamentally different business models -- IPP/asset-owners (ACME Solar, KPI Green via Sun Drops Energia, Inox Clean via the Vena Energy India acquisition) versus EPC/equipment suppliers (Pace Digitek, Enviro Infra) -- and cannot be scored as one entity.
fundamentals_table: Thematic/basket thread, not one listed company
411.4 GWh total (236.2 GWh BESS + 175.2 GWh pumped hydro); ~Rs2.65 lakh cr implied BESS capex need

fundamentals_narrative: The policy/funding backdrop is real and accelerating, not speculative: CEA's FY32 plan calls for 411.4 GWh of total storage (236.2 GWh BESS), government VGF support was extended via a second Rs5,400cr/30 GWh tranche on 14-May-2026 (on top of the original Sep-2023 Rs9,400cr tranche), and genuine commissioning activity is now visible -- ACME Solar alone reached 4.96 GWh of operational BESS capacity through 2026, with FDRE/assured-peak-power project structures that map directly onto this thread's own RTC/FDRE framing. But execution still lags intent industry-wide (~69 tenders/~102 GWh floated in 2025 vs just 758.4 MWh actually commissioned by year-end), and the thread itself resolves to at least 5 companies with different business models and risk profiles, so no single fundamentals_table can represent 'the' investment.
bull_case: BESS buildout is a confirmed, funded national priority, not a narrative: CEA's FY32 plan needs 411.4 GWh of total storage (236.2 GWh BESS) and ~Rs2.65 lakh cr capex; a second VGF tranche (Rs5,400cr for 30 GWh) was approved as recently as 14-May-2026, on top of the original Sep-2023 Rs9,400cr tranche

Real commissioning is happening, not just tendering: ACME Solar alone has 4.96 GWh of operational BESS capacity with explicit FDRE/assured-peak-power project structures directly matching this thread's own framing

Multiple entry points across the value chain have live, dated order books: IPP/asset owners (ACME Solar, KPI Green via Sun Drops Energia, Inox Clean via the Vena Energy India acquisition) and EPC/manufacturing plays (Pace Digitek scaling 2.5->10 GWh manufacturing capacity, Enviro Infra diversifying from water-treatment into BESS EPC)

Order books are large and real: Pace Digitek Rs11,338cr (incl. 5.32 GWh storage pipeline), KPI Green's Sun Drops Energia at 565MW/1,130MWh executed plus a 600MW/~Rs1,050cr RTC LOI, Enviro Infra's BESS-inclusive order book past Rs4,600cr
bear_case: This is not one stock -- it is at least a 5-company basket spanning fundamentally different business models (asset-owning IPPs vs EPC/equipment suppliers), different balance sheets, and different valuations; no single four-box or conviction call can honestly represent all of them

Industry-wide execution lags intent: ~69 BESS tenders (~102 GWh) floated in 2025 but only 758.4 MWh cumulatively commissioned by year-end -- a large gap between announced pipeline and delivered capacity across the sector

For the EPC-model proxies (Pace Digitek, Enviro Infra), BESS is a newly-entered, fast-growing but unproven-at-scale segment layered onto a different core business (Enviro Infra's core is water/wastewater treatment) -- execution risk on a new technology/segment is real

4 of 5 named proxies already have dedicated entries elsewhere in this project where their actual fundamentals, valuation, and risk are properly assessed -- continuing to carry this basket entry alongside those risks diluting analytical focus without adding distinct value
